A loose pile of plain paper slips sits on the left pan and an equal pile of plain paper slips sits on the right pan, and the beam is perfectly level. The agent holds both hands up, visibly stuck, unable to choose between them. Outside the laptop, in the warm real world, a woman in her thirties with black hair in a low bun and a mustard-yellow blouse watches the level scale.

BEAT TWO: The consequence. The same laptop and the same balance scale. The woman has reached in and set a small solid brass weight onto the LEFT pan, and that pan has sunk down while the right pan has risen up. The brass weight is engraved with a tiny lit-up open shopfront with its lights on and its door open. The agent watches the left pan sink. The tilted scale is the focus.

BEAT THREE: The resolution. Inside the laptop the agent stands beside the tilted scale holding up the thick stack of slips from the heavy left pan, looking clear and decided. Outside the laptop the woman has kept exactly THREE of the light slips from the right pan, held deliberately in her free hand down at the desk, not discarded.
